subject: Shiny testing - best practices and advice

messages.author: 2e1695c2061d5312
messages.subject: Shiny testing - best practices and advice
parts:
Our company uses several shiny apps which we have written, both on our own servers and using the shinyapps.io service.

We are trying to put in place automated testing for these. At an absolute minimum we would like to know that the right app is running at the right URL, and that it loads correctly (not greyed out on load, no error console). Ideally we would like to check much more - for example we want to click through all tabs to see that they load correctly, do some basic input, and check the output. We want to know about both bugs in our code or infrastructure problems such as incorrect database details before our customers do.

We have started writing selenium tests, both with RSelenium and selenium for Python. However we have found that writing good Selenium tests is tricky, and that a lot of work has to be done to get tests which are reasonably stable, and which give us meaningful results. Some of this seems to the normal work that Selenium requires to be used (ie finding all the right CSS selectors and checking the DOM after each UI interaction to check for elements which might have moved/disappeared/been replaced). Some of it seems to be related to the complexity of our pages and the Shiny UI elements, and some of it we think is unexpected behavior by Selenium. One example is that we have found it impossible in RSelenium to correctly interact with the Selectize Bootstrap widget in Shiny.

Is Selenium the best approach and is RSelenium the best others have found to test Shiny? Is there anything that we should know about when trying to write Selenium tests for Shiny code? Should we change how we write our app code to make Selenium testing work better?

I would be very happy to here from anyone who has any suggestions or can share there experiences, particularly if they have been successful in doing extensive automated testing of Shiny apps.

Thanks ia,
Jack Grahl

messages.subject: Re: Shiny testing - best practices and advice
parts: Following Dean's example ... I have only tried a few things with Rselenium and agree it is not particularly easy to use. One thing I have done is use 'regular' r-functions that are called from reactive functions as much as possible. That way I can at least test the 'regular' functions using testthat.
